title: What the Discovery Reactor is
description: The reactor systematically hunts for cross-domain combinations: it indexes methods by what they do (not what field they come from), matches unsolved problems to methods from other fields, and proposes transfers with explicit analogy mappings. Each proposal includes where the analogy is expected to break — honesty about limits is what makes the proposals testable.

title: Method and problem data model
description: Methods are recorded by their mechanism, inputs, outputs, assumptions, and known limits — not by their home field. Problems are recorded by their structure: constraints, goals, and failure modes. This field-blind representation is what lets a heat-transfer method match a finance problem: the structures align even when the vocabularies do not.

title: Breakdown prediction algorithm
